public_rationale: Marcus forecast many lab demos of humanoid robots in 2026, but great difficulty getting them to work in homes. The forecast window ends on 2026-12-31, which is after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. The only cited item is an eWeek report dated 2026-04-27 (e1). It said 1X NEO shipments were expected to begin in 2026 and that the rollout would serve as a real-world experiment for domestic robotics. This is consistent with the forecast, but it is context from April, not a year-end result. No item in the evidence shows independent reviews of reliable, autonomous household use in many homes, so the early-contradiction rule is not met on this record. Under the contract, support can only be judged after the year ends.
limitations: The evidence includes no independent 2026 home trials measuring task success, failures or human intervention.
The evidence does not count 2026 demos, so the 'tons of lab demos' part is not assessed.
The only cited item covers one company (1X), dated April 2026.
'Very very hard' and 'tons' have no thresholds, so the final call will need judgment.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: during 2026, there will be many demos of humanoid home robots, but few will work reliably in real homes. Home deployments will be scarce, limited, heavily assisted (for example teleoperated), or have documented reliability problems.
Early resolution rule: contradicted early if, before 2026-12-31, independent reviews document humanoid robots doing useful household tasks autonomously and reliably in many ordinary homes at scale.
criteria.support_condition: By the end of 2026, demos of humanoid home robots are plentiful, while real home use is rare, limited, heavily teleoperated or shown to be unreliable in independent reviews.
criteria.contradiction_condition: During 2026, humanoid robots are shown in independent reviews to work reliably and autonomously in many consumer homes, or demos are few.
